references.text: During the trial against Jesus, false witnesses testified that he had said: "I can destroy God's temple and rebuild it in three days" ([ref:Matt 26:61|Matthew 26:61]). This is a direct reference to Jesus' statement about the temple.

Those who passed by Jesus on the cross mocked him, saying: "You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days" ([ref:Matt 27:40|Matthew 27:40]), a distorted version of his words about the temple.

Also in Mark's account of the trial, false witnesses testify that Jesus said: "I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days build another not made with hands" ([ref:Mark 14:58|Mark 14:58]).
Also in Mark's crucifixion narrative, passersby mock Jesus with words about destroying the temple and rebuilding it in three days ([ref:Mark 15:29|Mark 15:29]).

John explains that the temple Jesus spoke of was his own body. The disciples understood this only after the resurrection ([ref:Joh 2:21-22|John 2:21-22]), which directly links the statement to Jesus' death and resurrection.
Stephen was accused of saying that "Jesus from Nazareth will destroy this place" ([ref:Apg 6:14|Acts 6:14]), an echo of Jesus' words about the temple.

Jesus uses the sign of Jonah as a prophecy of his resurrection on the third day: "For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth" ([ref:Matt 12:40|Matthew 12:40]). The three-day motif connects directly to the promise to raise the temple in three days.
Jesus openly predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection on the third day ([ref:Matt 16:21|Matthew 16:21]), which unfolds the meaning of the promise to raise up the temple in three days.

Jesus says that he has power to lay down his life and take it up again ([ref:Joh 10:17-18|John 10:17-18]). This corresponds with his words about raising up the temple, since by "temple" he meant his own body.

Paul writes: "Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit?" ([ref:1 Kor 6:19|1 Corinthians 6:19]). The idea of the body as a temple connects to Jesus' identification of his body as the temple.
